verses.text: The Book of the words of Tobit, son of Tobiel, the son of Ananiel, the son of Aduel, the son of Gabael, of the seed of Asael, of the Tribe of Nephthali,
Who in the time of Enemessar king of the Assyrians, was led captive out of This be which is at the right hand of that city, which is called properly Nephthali in Galile above Aser.
I Tobit have walked all the days of my life in the way of truth, and justice, and I did many alms deeds to my brethren, and my nation, who came with me to Nineveh into the land of the Assyrians.

And when I was in mine own country, in the land of Yahsharala, being but young, all the tribe of Nephthali my father, fell from the house of Jerusalem, which was chosen out of all the tribes of Yahsharala, that all the tribes should sacrifice there where the Temple of the habitation of the most High was consecrated, and built for all ages.
Now all the tribes which together revolted, and the house of my father Nephthali sacrificed to the heifer Baal.

But I alone went often to Jerusalem at the Feasts, as it was ordained to al the people of Yahsharala by an everlasting decree, having the first fruits, and tenths of encrease, with that which was first shorn, and them gave I at the Altar to the Priests the children of Aaron.
The first tenth part of al increase, I gave to the sons of Aaron, who ministered at Jerusalem: another tenth part I sold away, and went, and spent it every year at Jerusalem.
And the third, I gave to them to whom it was meet, as Debora my fathers mother had commanded me, because I was left an orphane by my father.
Furthermore when I was come to the age of a man, I married Anna of mine own kinred, and of her I begate Tobias.
And when we were caried away captives to Nineveh, all my brethren, and those that were of my kinred, did eat of the bread of the Gentiles.
But I kept my selfe from eating
Because I remembred Alahayam with all my heart.
And the most High gave me grace, and favor before Enemessar, so that I was his purueyour.
And I went into Media, and left in trust with Gabael, the brother of Gabrias at Rages a city of Media, ten talents of siluer.
Now when Enemessar was dead, Sennacherib his son reigned in his stead, whose estate was troubled, that I could not go into Media.
And in the time of Enemessar, I gave many alms to my brethren, and gave my bread to the hungry,
And my clothes to the naked: and if I saw any of my nation dead, or cast about the walles of Nineveh, I buried him.

And if the king Sennacherib had slaine any, when he was come, and fledde from Iudea, I buried them priuily, (for in his wrath he killed many) but the bodies were not found, when they were sought for of the king.
And when one of the Nineuites went, and complained of me to the king that I buried them, and hid my selfe: understanding that I was sought for to be put to death, I withdrew my selfe for fear.
Then all my goods were forcibly taken away, neither was there any thing left me, besides my wife Anna, and my son Tobias.

And there passed not five and fifty days before two of his sons killed him, and they fled into the mountaines of Ararath, and Sarchedonus his son reigned in his stead, who appointed over his fathers accounts, and over all his affaires, Achiacharus my brother Anaels son.

And Achiacharus entreating for me, I returned to Nineveh: now Achiacharus was Cup-bearer, and keeper of the Signet, and Steward, and ouerseer of the accounts: and Sarchedonus appointed him next to him: and he was my brothers son.

Now when I was come home again, and my wife Anna was restored to me, with my son Tobias, in the feast of Pentecost, which is the holy Feast of the seven weekes, there was a good dinner prepared me, in the which I sate down to eat.
And when I saw abundance of food, I said to my son, Go and bring what poor man soeuer you shall find out of our brethren, who is mindfull of the Lord, and loe, I tarie for you.
But he came again and said, Father, one of our nation is strangled, and is cast out in the market place.
Then before I had tasted of any food, I start up and tooke him up into a room, until the going downe of the Sunne.
Then I returned and washed my selfe, and ate my food in heauinesse,
Remembering that prophesie of Amos, as he said; Your feasts shall be turned into mourning, and all your mirth into lamentation.
Therefore I wept: and after the going downe of the Sunne, I went and made a graue, and buried him.
But my neighbours mocked me, and said, This man is not yet afraide to be put to death for this matter, who fledde away, and yet loe, he buries the dead again.
The same night also I returned from the buriall, and slept by the wall of my court yard, being polluted, and my face was vncouered:

And I knewe not that there were Sparrowes in the wall, and mine eyes being open, the Sparrowes muted warme doung into mine eyes, and a whitenesse came in mine eyes, and I went to the Physicians, but they helped me not: moreouer Achiacharus did nourish me, until I went into Elymais.
And my wife Anna did take womens workes to do.
And when she had sent them home to the owners, they paid her wages, and gave her also besides a kid.
And when it was in mine house, and began to crie, I said to her, From whence is this kidde? is it not stollen? render it to the owners, for it is not lawfull to eat any thing that is stollen.

But she replyed upon me, It was given for a gift more then the wages: Howbeit I did not believe her, but bade her render it to the owners: and I was abashed at her. But she replyed upon me, Where are yours alms, and your righteous deeds? behold, you and all your workes are known.
Then I being grieved, did weepe, and in my sorrowe prayed, saying,
O Lord, you are just and all your workes, and all your ways are mercy and truth, and you judge truely and justly for ever.
Remember me, and look on me, punish me not for my sins and ignorances, and the sins of my fathers, who have sinned before you.
For they obeyed not your commandments, therefore you have deliuered us for a spoile, and to captiuitie, and to death, and for a prouerbe of reproch to all the nations among whom we are dispersed.
And now your iudgments are many and true: Deale with me according to my sins, and my fathers: because we have not kept your commandments, neither have walked in truth before you.

Now therefore deale with me as seems best to you, and command my spirit to be taken from me, that I may be dissolued, and become earth: for it is profitable for me to die, rather then to live, because I have heard false reproches, and have much sorow: command therfore that I may now be deliuered out of this distresse, and go into the everlasting place: turne not your face away from me.
It came to pass the same day, that in Ecbatane a city of Media, Sara the daughter of Raguel, was also reproched by her fathers maides,

Because that she had bin maried to seven husbands, whom Almodeus the evil spirit had killed, before they had lien with her. Do you not know, said they, that you have strangled your husbands? you have had already seven husbands, neither were you named after any of them.
Why do you beate us for them? If they be dead, go your ways after them, let us never see of you either son or daughter.

When she heard these things, she was very sorowful, so that she thought to have strangled her selfe, and she said, I am the only daughter of my father, and if I do this, it shall be a reproch to him, and I shall bring his old age with sorow to the graue.
Then she prayed toward the window, and said, Blessed art you, O Lord my Alahayam, and your holy and glorious Name is blessed, and honourable foreuer, let al your works praise you for ever.
And now, O Lord, I set mine eyes and my face toward you,
And say, take me out of the earth, that I may hear no more the reproch.
You know, Lord, that I am pure from all sin with man,

And that I never polluted my name, nor the name of my father in the land of my captiuitie: I am the only daughter of my father, neither has he any child to be his heire, neither any neere kinseman, nor any son of his aliue, to whome I may keep my selfe for a wife: my seven husbands are already dead, and why should I live? but if it please not you that I should die, command some regard to be had of me, and pity taken of me, that I hear no more reproch.
So the prayers of them both were heard before the Maiesty of the great Alahayam.

And Raphael was sent to heale them both, that is, to scale away the whitenesse of Tobits eyes, and to give Sara the daughter of Raguel, for a wife to Tobias the son of Tobit, and to bind Asmodeus the evil spirit, because she belongs to Tobias by right of inheritance. The selfe same time came Tobit home, and entred into his house, and Sara, the daughter of Raguel came downe from her vpper chamber.
In that day Tobit remembred the money, which he had committed to Gabael in Rages of Media,
And said with himselfe, I have wished for death, why do I not call for my son Tobias, that I may signifie to him of the money before I die.
And when he had called him, he said; My son, when I am dead, bury me, and despise not your mother, but honor her all the days of your life, and do that which shall please her, and greiue her not.
Remember, my son, that she saw many dangers for you, when you were in her wombe, and when she is dead, bury her by me in one graue.

My son, be mindfull of the Lord our Alahayam all your days, and let not your will be set to sin, or to transgresse his Commandments: do vprightly all your life long, and follow not the ways of vnrighteousnesse.
For if you deale truely, your doings shall prosperously succeed to you, and to all them that live justly.
Give alms of your substance, and when you giuest alms, let not your eye be enuious, neither turne your face from any poor, and the face of Alahayam shall not be turned away from you.
If you have abundance, give alms accordingly: if you have but a litle, be not afraid to give according to that litle.
For you layest up a good treasure for your selfe against the day of necessitie.
Because that alms does deliuer from death, and suffers not to come into darknesse.
For alms is a good gift to all that give it, in the sight of the most High.

Beware of all whoredome, my son, and chiefely take a wife of the seed of your fathers, and take not a strange woman to wife, which is not of your fathers tribe: for we are the children of the Prophets, Noe, Abraham, Isaak, and Jacob: remember, my son, that our fathers from the beginning, even that they all maried wiues of their own kinred, and were blessed in their children, and their seede shall inherite the land.

Now therefore my son, love your brethren, and despise not in your heart your brethren, the sons and daughters of your people, in not taking a wife of them: for in pride is destruction and much trouble, and in lewdnesse is decay, and great want: for lewdnesse is the mother of famine.

Let not the wages of any man, which has wrought for you, tary with you, but give him it out of hand: for if you serve Alahayam he will also repay you: be circumspect, my son, in all things you do, and be wise in all your conuersation.
Do that to no man which you hatest: drinke not wine to make you drunken; neither let drunkennesse go with you in your journey.
Give of your bread to the hungry, and of your garments to them that are naked, and according to your abundance give alms, and let not your eye be enuious, when you giuest alms.
Power out your bread on the buriall of the just, but give nothing to the wicked.
Aske counsel of all that are wise, and despise not any counsel that is profitable.

Blesse the Lord your Alahayam alway, and desire of him that your ways may be directed, and that all your pathes, and counsels may prosper: for every nation has not counsel, but the Lord himselfe gives all good things, and he humbles whom he will, as he will; now therefore my son, remember my commandments, neither let them be put out of your minde.
And now I signifie this to you, that I committed tenne talents to Gabael the son of Gabrias at Rages in Media.
And fear not my son, that we are made poor, for you have much wealth, if you fear Alahayam, and depart from all sin, and do that which is pleasing in his sight.
Tobias then answered and said, Father, I will do all things, which you have commanded me.
But how can I receive the money, seeing, I know him not?
Then he gave him the handwriting, and said to him, Seeke you a man which may go with you whiles I yet live, and I will give him wages, and go, and receive the money.
Therefore when he went to seeke a man, he found Raphael that was an Angell.
But he knew not; and he said to him, Canst you go with me to Rages? and do you know those places well?
To whom the Angel said, I will go with you, and I know the way well: for I have lodged with our brother Gabael.
Then Tobias said to him, Tary for me until I tell my father.

Then he said to him, Go and tary not; so he went in, and said to his father; Behold, I have found one, which will go with me. Then he said, Call him to me, that I may know of what tribe he is, and whether he be a trustie man to go with you.
So he called him, and he came in, and they saluted one another.
Then Tobit said to him, Brother, show me of what tribe and family you are.
To whom he said, Do you seeke for a tribe or family, or an hired man to go with your son? Then Tobit said to him, I would know, brother, your kinred, and name.
Then he said, I am Azarias, the son of Ananias the great, and of your brethren.

Then Tobit said, You are welcome brother, be not now angry with me, because I have enquired to know your tribe, and your family, for you are my brother, of an honest and good stocke: for I know Ananias, and Ionathas sons of that great Samaias: as we went together to Jerusalem to worship, and offered the first borne, and the tenths of the fruits, and they were not seduced with the errour of our brethren: my brother, you are of a good stocke.
But tell me, what wages shall I give you? will you accept a drachma a day? and things necessary as to my own son?
Yea moreouer, if you returne safe, I will adde some thing to the wages.

So they were well pleased. Then said he to Tobias; Prepare your selfe for the journey, and Alahayam send you a good journey. And when his son had prepared all things for the journey, his father said; Go you with this man, and Alahayam which dwells in heaven prosper your journey, and the Angel of Alahayam keep you company. So they went foorth both, and the young mans dogge with them.
But Anna his mother wept, and said to Tobit, Why have you sent away our son? is he not the staffe of our hand, in going in and out before us?
Be not greedy (to adde) money to money: but let it be as refuse in respect of our childe.
For that which the Lord has given us to live with, does suffice us.
Then said Tobit to her, Take no care my sister he shall returne in safety, and your eyes shall see him.
For the good Angel will keep him company, and his journey shall be prosperous, and he shall returne safe.
Then she made an end of weeping.
And as they went on their journey, they came in the euening to the riuer Tigris, and they lodged there.
And when the young man went downe to wash himselfe, a fish leaped out of the riuer, and would have deuoured him.
Then the Angel said to him, Take the fish; and the young man layd hold of the fish, and drew it to land.
To whom the Angel said, Open the fish, and take the heart, and the liuer and the gall, and put them up safely.
So the young man did as the Angel commanded him, and when they had rosted the fish, they did eat it: then they both went on their way, until they drew neere to Ecbatane.
Then the young man saide to the Angel; Brother Azarias, to what use is the heart, and the liuer, and the gall of the fish?
And he said to him, Touching the heart and the liuer, if a deuil, or an evil spirit trouble any, we must make a smoke thereof before the man or the woman, and the party shalbe no more vexed.
As for the gall it is good to anoint a man that has whitenesse in his eyes, and he shalbe healed.
And when they were come neere to Rages;
The Angel said to the young man, Brother, to day we shall lodge with Raguel, who is your cousin; he also has one only daughter, named Sara, I will speak for her, that she may be given you for a wife.
For to you does the right of her appertaine, seeing you only art of her kinred.

And the maide is faire and wise, now therefore hear me, and I will speak to her father, and when we returne from Rages, we will celebrate the mariage: for I know that Raguel cannot marry her to another according to the Law of Moses, but he shalbe guiltie of death, because the right of inheritance does rather appertaine to you, then to any other.
Then the young man answered the Angel, I have heard, brother Azarias, that this maide has been given to seven men, who all died in the marriage chamber:

And now I am the only son of my father, and I am afraid, lest if I go in to her, I die, as the other before; for a wicked spirit loves her, which hurts no body, but those which come to her; therefore I also fear, lest I die, and bring my fathers and my mothers life (because of me) to the graue with sorrow, for they have no other son to bury them.

Then the Angel said to him, Do you not remember the precepts, which your father gave you, that you should marrie a wife of your own kindred? therefore hear me, O my brother, for she shall be given you to wife, and make you no reckoning of the evil spirit, for this same night shall she be given you in mariage.
And when you shall come into the mariage chamber, you shall take the ashes of perfume, and shall lay upon them, some of the heart, and liuer of the fish, and shall make a smoke with it.

And the deuill shall smell it, and flee away, and never come again any more: but when you shall come to her, rise up both of you, and pray to Alahayam, which is mercifull, who will have pity on you, and saue you: fear not, for she is appointed to you from the beginning; and you shall preserue her, and she shall go with you. Moreouer I suppose that she shall beare you children. Now when Tobias had heard these things, he loued her, and his heart was effectually ioyned to her.
And when they were come to Ecbatane, they came to the house of Raguel; and Sara met them: and after that they had saluted one another, she brought them into the house.
Then said Raguel to Edna his wife, How like is this young man to Tobit my cousin?
And Raguel asked them, From whence are you, brethren? To whom they said, We are of the sons of Nephthali, which are captives in Nineveh.
Then he said to them, Do you know Tobit our kinseman? And they said, We know him. Then said he, Is he in good health?
And they said, He is both aliue, and in good health: And Tobias said, He is my father.
Then Raguel leaped up, and kissed him, and wept,
And blessed him; and said to him, You are the son of an honest and good man: but when he had heard that Tobit was blinde, he was sorowfull, and wept.

And likewise Edna his wife, and Sara his daughter wept. Moreouer, they entertained them cheerefully, and after that they had killed a ramme of the flocke, they served plenty of meat on the table. Then said Tobias to Raphael, Brother Azarias, speak of those things, of which you did talke in the way, and let this businesse be dispatched.
So he communicated the matter with Raguel, and Raguel said to Tobias, Eat and drink, and make merry:
For it is meet that you should marry my daughter: nevertheless I will declare to you the truth.

I have given my daughter in mariage to seven men, who died that night they came in to her: nevertheless for the present be merry: But Tobias said, I will eat nothing here, until we agree and sweare one to another.
Raguel said, Then take her from hencefoorth according to the manner, for you are her cousin, and she is yours, and the mercifull Alahayam give you good successe in all things.

Then he called his daughter Sara, and she came to her father, and he tooke her by the hand, and gave her to be wife to Tobias, saying, Behold, take her after the Law of Moses, and leade her away to your father: And he blessed them,
And called Edna his wife, and tooke paper, and did write an instrument of couenants, and sealed it.
Then they began to eat.
After Raguel called his wife Edna, and said to her, Sister, prepare another chamber, and bring her in there.
Which when she had done as he had bidden her, she brought her there, and she wept, and she received the teares of her daughter, and said to her,
Be of good comfort, my daughter, the Lord of heaven and earth give you ioy for this your sorow: be of good comfort, my daughter.
And when they had supped, they brought Tobias in to her.
And as he went, he remembred the words of Raphael, and tooke the ashes of the perfumes, and put the heart, and the liuer of the fish thereupon, and made a smoke therewith.
The which smell, when the evil spirit had smelled, he fled into the outmost parts of Egypt, and the Angel bound him.
And after that they were both shut in together, Tobias rose out of the bed and said, Sister, arise, and let us pray, that Alahayam would have pity on us.
Then began Tobias to say, Blessed art you, O Alahayam of our fathers, and blessed is your holy and glorious Name for ever, let the heavens blesse you, and all your creatures.
You madest Adam, and gauest him Eue his wife for an helper and stay: of them came mankind: you have said, It is not good that man should be alone, let us make to him an aide like to himselfe.
And now, O Lord, I take not this my sister for lust, but vprightly: therefore mercifully ordeine, that we may become aged together.
And she said with him, Amen.
So they slept both that night, and Raguel arose, and went and made a graue
Saying, I fear lest he be dead.
But when Raguel was come into his house,
He said to his wife Edna, Send one of the maids, and let her see, whether he be aliue: if he be not, that we may bury him, and no man know it.
So the maid opened the doore and went in, and found them both asleepe,
And came forth, and told them, that he was aliue.

Then Raguel praised Alahayam, and said, O Alahayam, you are worthy to be praised with all pure and holy praise: therefore let your Saints praise you with all your creatures, and let all your Angels and your elect praise you for ever.
You are to be praised, for you have made me ioyfull, and that is not come to me, which I suspected: but you have dealt with us according to your great mercy.
You are to be praised, because you have had mercy of two, that were the only begotten children of their fathers, grant them mercy, O Lord, and finish their life in health, with ioy and mercy.
Then Raguel bade his servants to fill the graue.
And he kept the wedding feast fourteene days.
For before the days of the mariage were finished, Raguel had said to him by an othe, that he should not depart, until the fourteene days of the mariage were expired,
And then he should take the halfe of his goods, and go in safetie to his father, and should have the rest when I and my wife be dead.
Then Tobias called Raphael, and said to him,
Brother Azarias, Take with you a servant, and two camels, and go to Rages of Media to Gabael, and bring me the money, and bring him to the wedding.
For Raguel has sworne that I shall not depart.
But my father counts the days, and if I tarie long, he will be very sorie.
So Raphael went out and lodged with Gabael, and gave him the handwriting, who brought forth bags, which were sealed up, and gave them to him.
And earely in the morning they went forth both together, and came to the wedding, and Tobias blessed his wife.
Nowe Tobit his father counted every day, and when the days of the journey were expired, and they came not:
Then Tobit said, Are they detained? or is Gabael dead? and there is no man to give him the money?
Therefore he was very sory.
Then his wife said to him, My son is dead, seeing he stays long, and she began to bewaile him, and said,
Now I care for nothing, my son, since I have let you go, the light of mine eyes.
To whom Tobit said, Hold your peace, take no care; for he is safe.

But she said, Hold your peace, and deceiue me not: my son is dead, and she went out every day into the way which they went, and ate no food during the day, and ceased not whole nights, to bewaile her son Tobias, until the fourteen days of the wedding were expired, which Raguel had sworne, that he should spend there: Then Tobias said to Raguel, Let me go, for my father, and my mother look no more to see me.
But his father in law said to him, Tary with me, and I will send to your father, and they shall declare to him, how things go with you.
But Tobias said, No: but let me go to my father.
Then Raguel arose and gave him Sara his wife, and halfe his goods, servants, and cattell, and money.
And he blessed them, and sent them away, saying, The Alahayam of heaven give you a prosperous journey, my children.

And he said to his daughter, Honor your father and your mother in law, which are now your parents, that I may hear good report of you: and he kissed her. Edna also said to Tobias, The Lord of heaven restore you, my dear brother, and grant that I may see your children of my daughter Sara before I die, that I may rejoice before the Lord: behold, I commit my daughter to you of speciall trust, therefore do not entreate her evil.
After these things Tobias went his way, praising Alahayam that he had given him a prosperous journey, and blessed Raguel, and Edna his wife, and went on his way until they drew neere to Nineveh.
Then Raphael said to Tobias, You know brother, how you did leave your father.
Let us haste before your wife, and prepare the house.
And take in your hand the gall of the fish: so they went their way, and the dog went after them.
Now Anna sate looking about towards the way for her son.
And when she espied him comming, she said to his father, Behold, your son comes, and the man that went with him.
Then said Raphael, I know, Tobias, that your father will open his eyes.
Therefore annoint you his eies with the gall, and being pricked therewith he shall rub, and the whitenesse shall fall away, and he shall see you.
Then Anna ran forth, and fell upon the necke of her son, and said to him, seeing I have seene you my son, from henceforth, I am content to die, and they wept both.
Tobit also went forth toward the doore, and stumbled: but his son ran to him,
And tooke hold of his father, and he strake of the gall on his fathers eyes, saying, Be of good hope, my father.
And when his eyes began to smart, he rubbed them.
And the whitenesse pilled away from the corners of his eyes, and when he saw his son, he fell upon his necke.
And he wept, and said, Blessed art you, O Alahayam, and blessed is your Name for ever, and blessed are all your holy Angels:
For you have scourged, and have taken pity on me: for behold, I see my son Tobias. And his son went in reioycing, and told his father the great things that had happened to him in Media.
Then Tobit went out to meete his daughter in law at the gate of Niniue, reioycing and praysing Alahayam: and they which saw him go, marueiled because he had received his sight.

But Tobit gave thankes before them: because Alahayam had mercy on him. And when he came neere to Sara his daughter in Law, he blessed her, saying, You are welcome daughter: Alahayam be blessed which has brought you to us, and blessed be your father and your mother; And there was ioy amongst all his brethren which were at Nineveh.
And Achiacharus, and Nasbas his brothers son came.
And Tobias wedding was kept seven days with great ioy.
Then Tobit called his son Tobias, and said to him, My son, see that the man have his wages, which went with you, and you must give him more.
And Tobias said to him, O father, it is no harme to me to give him halfe of those things which I have brought.
For he has brought me again to you in safety, and made whole my wife, and brought me the money, and likewise healed you.
Then the old man said: It is due to him.
So he called the Angell, and he said to him, Take halfe of all that you have brought, and go away in safety.

Then he tooke them both apart, and said to them, Blesse Alahayam, praise him, and magnifie him, and praise him for the things which he has done to you in the sight of all that live. It is good to praise Alahayam and exalt his name, and honorably to show forth the works of Alahayam, therfore be not slacke to praise him.
It is good to keep close the secret of a King, but it is honorable to reueale the works of Alahayam: do that which is good, and no evil shall touch you.
Prayer is good with fasting, and alms and righteousness: a little with righteousnes is better then much with vnrighteousnesse: it is better to give alms then to lay up gold.
For alms does deliuer from death, and shall purge away all sin. Those that exercise alms, and righteousness, shall be filled with life.
But they that sin are enemies to their own life.
Surely I will keep close nothing from you. For I said, it was good to keep close the secret of a King, but that it was honorable to reueale the works of Alahayam.
Now therefore, when you did pray, and Sara your daughter in Law, I did bring the remembrance of your prayers before the holy one, and when you did bury the dead, I was with you likewise.
And when you did not delay to rise up, and leave your dinner to go and couer the dead, your good deed was not hidde from me: but I was with you.
And now Alahayam has sent me to heale you, and Sara your daughter in law.
I am Raphael one of the seven holy Angels, which present the prayers of the Saints, and which go in and out before the glory of the Holy one.
Then they were both troubled, and fel upon their faces: for they feared.
But he said to them, fear not, for it shall go well with you, praise Alahayam therefore.
For not of any favor of mine, but by the will of our Alahayam I came, therefore praise him for ever.
All these days I did appeare to you, but I did neither eat nor drinke, but you did see a vision.
Now therefore give Alahayam thanks: for I go up to him who sent me, but write all things which are done, in a book.
And when they rose, they saw him no more.
Then they confessed the great and wonderfull workes of Alahayam, and how the Angel of the Lord had appeared to them.
Then Tobit wrote a prayer of reioycing, and said, Blessed be Alahayam that lives for ever, and blessed be his kingdom:
For he does scourge, and has mercy: he leads downe to hell, and brings up again: neither is there any that can auoid his hand.
Confesse him before the Gentiles, you children of Yahsharala: for he has scattered us among them.
There declare his greatnesse, and extoll him before all the living, for he is our Lord, and he is the Alahayam our father for ever:
And he will scourge us for our iniquities, and will have mercy again, and will gather us out of all nations, among whom he has scattered us.

If you turne to him with your whole heart, and with your whole minde, and deale vprightly before him, then will he turne to you, and will not hide his face from you: Therefore see what he will do with you, and confesse him with your whole mouth, and praise the Lord of might, and extoll the everlasting King: in the land of my captiuitie do I praise him, and declare his might and maiesty to a sinnefull nation: O you sinners turne, and do justice before him: who can tell if he will accept you, and have mercy on you?
I will extoll my Alahayam, and my soul shall praise the King of heaven, and shall rejoice in his greatnesse.
Let all men speak, and let all praise him for his righteousness.
O Jerusalem the holy City, he will scourge you for your childrens workes, and will have mercy again on the sons of the righteous.

Give praise to the Lord, for he is good: and praise the everlasting King, that his Tabernacle may be builded in you again with ioy: and let him make ioyfull there in you, those that are captives, and love in you for ever those that are miserable.
Many nations shall come from farre to the Name of the Lord Alahayam, with gifts in their hands, even giftes to the King of heaven: all generations shall praise you with great ioy.
Cursed are all they which hate you, and blessed shall all be, which love you for ever.
Rejoice and be glad for the children of the just: for they shall be gathered together, and shall blesse the Lord of the just.

O blessed are they which love you, for they shall rejoice in your peace: blessed are they which have been sorowfull for all your scourges, for they shall rejoice for you, when they have seene all your glory, and shalbe glad for ever.
Let my soul blesse Alahayam the great King.
For Jerusalem shall be built up with Saphires, and Emerauds, and precious stone: your walles and towres, and battlements with pure golde.
And the streets of Jerusalem shall be paued with Berill, and Carbuncle, and stones of Ophir.
And all her streets shall say, Halleluiah, and they shall praise him, saying, Blessed be Alahayam which has extolled it for ever.
So Tobit made an ende of praising Alahayam.
And he was eight and fifty years olde when he lost his sight, which was restored to him after eight years, and he gave alms, and he increased in the fear of the Lord Alahayam, and praised him.
And when he was very aged, he called his son, and the six sons of his son, and said to him, My son, take your children; for behold, I am aged, and am ready to depart out of this life.

Go into Media, my son, for I surely believe those things which Ionas the Prophet spoke of Nineveh, that it shall be ouerthrowen, and that for a time peace shall rather be in Media, and that our brethren shall lie scattered in the earth from that good land, and Jerusalem shall be desolate, and the house of Alahayam in it shalbe burned, and shall be desolate for a time:

And that again Alahayam will have mercy on them, and bring them again into the land where they shall build a Temple, but not like to the first, until the time of that age be fulfilled, and afterward they shall returne from all places of their captiuitie, and build up Jerusalem gloriously, and the house of Alahayam shall be built in it for ever, with a glorious building, as the prophets have spoken thereof.
And all nations shall turne, and fear the Lord Alahayam truely, and shall burie their idoles.

So shall all nations praise the Lord, and his people shall confesse Alahayam, and the Lord shall exalt his people, and all those which love the Lord Alahayam in truth and justice, shall rejoice, showing mercy to our brethren.
And now, my son, depart out of Nineveh, because that those things which the Prophet Ionas spoke, shall surely come to pass.
But keep you the Law and the Commandments, and show your selfe mercifull and just, that it may go well with you.

And burie me decently, and your mother with me, but tarie no longer at Nineveh. Remember, my son, how Aman handled Achiacharus who brought him up, how out of light he brought him into darkenes, and how he rewarded him again: yet Ahiacharus was saued, but the other had his reward, for he went downe into darkenesse. Manasses gave alms, and escaped the snares of death which they had set for him: but Aman fell into the snare and perished.

Therefore now, my son, consider what alms does, and how righteousness does deliuer. When he had said these things, he gave up the ghost in the bed, being a hundred, and eight and fifty years old, and he buried him honourably.
And when Anna his mother was dead, he buried her with his father: but Tobias departed with his wife and children to Ecbatane, to Raguel his father in law:
Where he became old with honor, and he buried his father and mother in lawe honourably, and he inherited their substance, and his father Tobits.
And he died at Ecbatane in Media, being a hundred and seven and twentie years old.
But before he died, he heard of the destruction of Nineveh, which was taken by Nabuchodonosor and Assuerus: and before his death he rejoiced over Nineveh.
